name: cdx_toolkit
what_it_holds: Python library + `cdxt` CLI that unifies querying Common Crawl's per-crawl CDX indices AND the Internet Archive Wayback Machine CDX API behind one interface. Can iterate captures across all Common Crawl monthly crawls for a URL/domain pattern, do size estimation, and pull matching WARC records to local WARC/JSONL/CSV. Apache-2.0, 287 commits, actively maintained.
why_useful: We already hold a Common Crawl CDX index over airbnb.com (2.08M rows); this tool would let us extend the same CDX-query workflow to the Wayback Machine's own (larger, longer-history) CDX index for airbnb.com, AirDNA, Mashvisor or insideairbnb.com without hand-rolling API calls, and pull matching WARC pages for gaps #1/#2.
last_activity: unspecified, beta but actively maintained per README
time_coverage: Common Crawl (2008-present) + full Wayback CDX depth
duplicate_of_holding: extends our existing Common Crawl CDX holding to the Wayback Machine index
themes: Wayback Machine / Internet Archive tooling and archived-page datasets (archived airbnb.com pages, archived AirDNA/Mashvisor market pages, archived Inside Airbnb site)
Common Crawl tooling: cdx-toolkit, warcio, host-level indexes, columnar index queries; datasets derived from Common Crawl for travel sites
why_all: We already hold a Common Crawl CDX index over airbnb.com (2.08M rows); this tool would let us extend the same CDX-query workflow to the Wayback Machine's own (larger, longer-history) CDX index for airbnb.com, AirDNA, Mashvisor or insideairbnb.com without hand-rolling API calls, and pull matching WARC pages for gaps #1/#2.

This is the direct successor/complement to the CDX capture already in hand (2.08M rows over airbnb.com, 50 crawls). Using cdx_toolkit against the Wayback CDX API (not just CC) would let us pull historical archived airbnb.com and AirDNA market pages point-in-time (gap 17, and supports gap 1/2 by finding old cached listing/price pages) without any new scraping infrastructure -- it is a public, ToS-neutral archive read, not a live site scrape.

name: Ceres
what_it_holds: Rust 'harvest-first' toolkit that syncs metadata from 300+ open-data portals (CKAN e.g. dati.comune.milano.it, DCAT/udata e.g. data.gouv.fr, DCAT-SPARQL e.g. data.europa.eu, Socrata e.g. data.cityofnewyork.us, OpenDataSoft e.g. opendata.paris.fr, ArcGIS Hub e.g. opendata.dc.gov, OGC/CSW, STAC, SDMX) into a normalized PostgreSQL catalog (2M+ datasets indexed), with reproducible Parquet snapshots published to Hugging Face (dataset AndreaBozzo/ceres-open-data-index, ~8.24MB, updated ~26 days ago) and optional semantic search via pgvector/Ollama/Gemini/OpenAI. Apache-2.0, 13 stars/4 forks/280 commits, actively developed Sep 2026.
why_useful: Directly answers the theme's core need — a working cross-portal discovery layer spanning exactly the Socrata/CKAN/OpenDataSoft/ArcGIS/DCAT universe named in CONTEXT.md gap #17 (Socrata/CKAN open-data discovery clients to find STR datasets across cities) and gap #12 (STR ordinance/registration datasets across many named cities). Its own metadata index (or the HF Parquet snapshot) could be queried offline to locate STR registries, tourism-board portals, or municipal lodging-tax data for the 20+ specific cities/countries in gaps 7, 8, 9, 12 without hitting live portals one at a time.
geography: global (300+ portals: US, EU, Italy, France, etc.)
themes: Open-data portal discovery: Socrata/CKAN/data.gov/EU data portal clients, dataset search tools, Google Dataset Search scrapers; city portals with STR datasets
why_all: Directly answers the theme's core need — a working cross-portal discovery layer spanning exactly the Socrata/CKAN/OpenDataSoft/ArcGIS/DCAT universe named in CONTEXT.md gap #17 (Socrata/CKAN open-data discovery clients to find STR datasets across cities) and gap #12 (STR ordinance/registration datasets across many named cities). Its own metadata index (or the HF Parquet snapshot) could be queried offline to locate STR registries, tourism-board portals, or municipal lodging-tax data for the 20+ specific cities/countries in gaps 7, 8, 9, 12 without hitting live portals one at a time.

name: Tcomp-r-package
what_it_holds: R package (`Tcomp`, installable via devtools::install_github) that ships the full dataset from the 2011 Tourism Forecasting Competition (Athanasopoulos, Hyndman, Song & Wu, Int'l J. Forecasting 2011): 1,311 time series of tourism-related indicators (visitor numbers, occupancy-adjacent series) across yearly, quarterly ($M1..$M...) and monthly ($M4 etc.) frequencies, stored as R Mcomp/Mdata objects (list `tourism`) rather than CSV. GPL-3.0, 6 stars, last updated 2025-03-20 (actively maintained wrapper around a fixed historical competition dataset).
why_useful: This is the canonical academic tourism-forecasting benchmark dataset (real submitted tourism arrivals/demand series across many countries) — directly answers the theme's core ask. Useful less as an ABNB predictor and more as a methods testbed: it is the standard corpus for validating hierarchical/reconciliation and ensemble forecasting techniques (gap 17, methods) that the team could apply to nights/ADR quarterly forecasting.
geography: Global (many countries, unspecified per-series in metadata)
time_coverage: Pre-2010 tourism series (submitted for the 2010 competition), multiple frequencies
size_hint: 1,311 series, small (R package, likely a few MB)
themes: Time-series datasets curated for tourism forecasting research (Monash, M-competitions tourism, Kaggle tourism forecasting), tourism demand models with data
why_all: This is the canonical academic tourism-forecasting benchmark dataset (real submitted tourism arrivals/demand series across many countries) — directly answers the theme's core ask. Useful less as an ABNB predictor and more as a methods testbed: it is the standard corpus for validating hierarchical/reconciliation and ensemble forecasting techniques (gap 17, methods) that the team could apply to nights/ADR quarterly forecasting.

This is the actual academic tourism-forecasting benchmark (not the well-known Kaggle Airbnb NYC file) with 1,311 real tourism series and both training/holdout splits used for point forecast accuracy competitions — directly on-theme for evaluating our own nights/ADR forecasting methodology against an established out-of-sample discipline (gap #17, methods: nowcasting/backtesting rigor), though the series themselves are generic tourism (arrivals/occupancy), not ABNB-specific.

name: jsvine/waybackpack
what_it_holds: Pure-Python (single dependency: requests) CLI to bulk-download every Wayback Machine snapshot of a given URL/URL pattern within a date range into timestamped local directories. MIT, 3.2k stars, 114 commits, 213 forks.
why_useful: Directly implements the 'Wayback Machine tooling (archived airbnb.com pages, archived AirDNA market pages)' method named in gap #17; could be pointed at archived insideairbnb.com/get-the-data pages or historical AirDNA market-report pages to recover CSVs/snapshots the CDN no longer serves.

name: hartator/wayback-machine-downloader
what_it_holds: Ruby gem (5.9k stars, 293 commits, MIT) that downloads an entire archived website (all pages, all timestamps or a filtered range) from the Wayback Machine, rebuilding the original directory/URL structure rather than IA's rewritten links.
why_useful: Alternative implementation of the same Wayback-mirroring method as waybackpack (gap #17); could recover archived insideairbnb.com data pages or AirDNA market pages.
